intro.en: Plotting and interpreting weight and height for age charts for girls and boys.

items.summary: Plotting a child weight against age on separate girls and boys charts to detect underweight early and grade its severity.

blocks.title: Which charts
bullets: Use the weight for age chart for girls for a girl child.
Use the weight for age chart for boys for a boy child.

blocks.title: How to plot and read
bullets: Mark age on the horizontal axis and weight on the vertical axis, then join the dots across visits.
A line tracking along its curve means steady gain; flattening or dipping warns of faltering.
Read the nearest coloured band or standard deviation (SD) line for the grade.

blocks.title: Cutoffs used with these charts
bullets: Weight below minus 2 SD for age marks underweight.
Weight below minus 3 SD marks severe underweight.

viva.q: Which chart do you pick for a 3 year old girl?
viva.a: The weight for age chart for girls.

viva.q: What does a flattening line warn of?
viva.a: Growth faltering needing feeding and illness review.
Below minus 2 SD underweight; below minus 3 SD severe.

image.brief: Weight for age growth chart for young children with curved percentile bands rising left to right, age along the bottom and weight up the side, one plotted dot joined to a flat warning line.

unsure: The book prints only the chart pictures with no cutoffs or plotting steps; the minus 2 SD and minus 3 SD cutoffs are standard WHO practice, added for the reviewer to confirm.

title.en: Length and height for age charts

items.summary: Tracking linear growth on separate girls and boys charts, measuring length lying down under 2 years and height standing after that.

blocks.title: Which charts
bullets: Use the length or height for age chart for girls for a girl child.
Use the length or height for age chart for boys for a boy child.

blocks.title: How to plot and read
bullets: Measure lying length under 2 years and standing height from 2 years on.
Mark age across and length or height upwards, then join the dots across visits.
A line drifting down across bands means chronic undernutrition (stunting).

blocks.title: Cutoffs used with these charts
bullets: Length or height below minus 2 SD for age marks stunting.
Length or height below minus 3 SD marks severe stunting.

viva.q: When do you switch from length to height?
viva.a: Lying length under 2 years, standing height from 2 years.

viva.q: What does a downward drift across bands mean?

viva.a: Below minus 2 SD stunting; below minus 3 SD severe.

image.brief: Length and height for age growth chart with curved bands, a tape measure icon showing lying measurement for infants and standing measurement for older children, one plotted line drifting down.

unsure: The book prints only the chart pictures with no cutoffs or plotting steps; the minus 2 SD and minus 3 SD cutoffs and the length to height switch at 2 years are standard WHO practice, added for the reviewer to confirm.
